offers.title: Firebase free allowances (Firestore / Auth / Hosting)
offers.freePlan: No-cost allowances (Spark and Blaze plans differ in meaning)
offers.storage: Firestore 1 GiB storage; Hosting 10 GB storage; Realtime Database 1 GB storage
offers.specText: Firestore: 1 GiB storage, 10 GiB outbound/month, 20K writes/day, 50K reads/day, 20K deletes/day; Auth: 50K MAU (SAML/OIDC 50); Hosting: 10 GB storage + 360 MB transfer per day, overage $0.15/GB; Realtime Database: 100 concurrent connections, 1 GB storage, 360 MB downloads/day (about 10 GB/month), overage $1/GB; Cloud Functions (Blaze column): 2M invocations/month, 400K GB-s, 200K CPU-s, 5 GB outbound, Spark column Not applicable; Cloud Storage free allowances in the Blaze column, Spark column Not applicable
offers.durationText: No-cost allowances; Spark and Blaze differ in meaning, see the detail page
offers.cardNote: Whether the Spark plan needs a payment method: second-hand statements say no payment method is needed, not directly confirmed in the captured official pricing page and FAQ — check the official page. The Blaze plan requires a billing account; Cloud Functions needs a billing account.
offers.idlePolicy: Idle-pause rules are not stated on the official pages read — check the official page.
offers.overage: Spark: exceeding any plan limit disables the app. Blaze: free allowances are calculated daily; no hard usage cap can be set.
offers.upgrade: Blaze pay-as-you-go + equivalent daily-calculated free allowances
risks: Spark overage disables the app: when you exceed any plan limit in any month, your app will be turned off (official FAQ wording)
Blaze cannot cap usage: No, you cannot currently cap your Blaze plan usage. (official FAQ wording)
Cloud Functions and Cloud Storage free allowances sit in the Blaze column; the Spark column reads Not applicable; Cloud Functions needs a billing account
Hosting free transfer is 360 MB/day; 10 GB/month is the equivalent expression for Realtime Database downloads — the two must not be mixed
offers.steps: Confirm each product's no-cost allowances and the Spark/Blaze meanings on the Firebase official pricing page → Create an account → Create a project and pick the products needed (Firestore, Auth, Hosting, Realtime Database) → Check daily usage in the console.
